O.outcome_detail: whether code generated in the first model response succeeded

cells.quote: InP3, the model was not significant, 𝜒 2 = 1.948,p= .378, indicating initial prompting method did not explain immediate success.
cells.note: The study reports a non-significant omnibus comparison among unedited voice, edited voice, and text prompting for P3; it does not report separate pairwise effects.

O.outcome_detail: proportion of time in focused attention during sustained-attention free play

cells.quote: There was a significant negative association between target P3 latencies and the proportion of time focused during the sustained attention task (r[16]=−.51, p=.032), such that children with longer P3 latencies demonstrated less sustained attention.
cells.note: The study measured the sustained-attention task and ERP on different days, approximately a week apart.

D.treatment: more irregular sleep timing and duration
D.comparison: less irregular sleep timing and duration

cells.quote: Additionally, results demonstrated a significant positive association between target P3 latencies and irregular sleep (r[18]=.61, p=.004), such that children with sleep that varied from night to night in timing and duration had longer target P3 latencies.
cells.note: The direction is coded as worse because greater irregularity was associated with longer P3 latency, described by the study as less efficient attentional processing.

cells.quote: The toddlers recognized the deviant target stimuli, responding to a greater percentage of target than frequent trials (t[19]=−4.38, p<.001).
cells.note: The target-versus-frequent contrast was measured within the auditory Oddball task.

cells.note: The study reports a phase × context interaction, with a steeper P3-amplitude decline across learning-phase blocks in the joint context; the contrast is not a simple overall joint-versus-baseline mean difference.

cells.note: Post-tests occurred immediately, 20 days, and 90 days after training.

cells.quote: After training, the accuracy was signiﬁcantly increased, the response time signiﬁcantly decreased, and these performance changes were maintained for at least 90 days after training.
cells.note: The detailed results also report some post-training slowing over follow-up, so durability varies by task and time point.

O.outcome_detail: task-evoked P300 global field power and topographic distribution

cells.quote: The ERP results provided strong evidence that training signiﬁcantly enhanced P300 responses, with a more pronounced increase in P300 GFP and a shift in topographic distribution observed 20days after training.
cells.note: The study interprets the channelwise and topographic changes as altered neural processing, but the outcome is an EEG measure rather than learning performance.
